summary: WAF cookie affinity injects Set-Cookie and downgrades HTTP/2 -> HTTP/1.1, causing intermittent streaming 401s and gRPC resets on private deployment
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent 401 Unauthorized responses and abrupt streaming resets when performing long-running generation requests against their Private deployment (VPCE in us-east-1). The failures started after a corporate WAF/NGFW appliance was rolled out in front of the branch office network (customer side).

Impact:
- Multiple model streams aborted (~5-10% of requests during peak).
- Token refresh and KV-cache misses observed leading to higher tail latency and occasional 401s.
- Customer-facing ML feature degraded during nightly batch of long outputs.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPCE) with regional serving nodes in us-east-1
- Customer network: branch office behind on-prem WAF that performs HTTP inspection and cookie injection
- Client SDK: Redwood JS v2.14.0 using streaming gRPC over HTTP/2

Steps to reproduce:
1) From customer branch, initiate a long streaming generate call (>60s).
2) Observe stream for ~30-90s: sometimes connection is reset and client logs 401s on subsequent short replays.
3) Reproduce more reliably by sending concurrent long-lived streams (10 concurrent).

Observed behavior / logs:
- Client-side: grpc: received RST_STREAM followed by http2: server sent GOAWAY code=NO_ERROR on stream
- Serving node logs: auth token validated on initial connect, subsequent requests from same client identity returned 401 with header "x-session-reset: true"
- VPCE logs: many upstream requests appear as HTTP/1.1 POST with Connection: close and Set-Cookie headers inserted by an intermediate appliance
- Packet traces (p-capture from customer) show ALPN negotiation initially advertises h2; some subsequent TCP connections re-establish with HTTP/1.1 due to WAF re-serialization

Initial customer workaround attempted:
- Customer disabled the WAF cookie-injection profile and reported immediate reduction of failures.
- Temporary bypass of inspection for traffic to Redwood endpoints also reduced failures.

Notes: this ticket documents the cross-team investigation and proposed remediation.
comments: 2026-03-10 14:05 - Support (Aisha): Ticket created after customer report. Asking for packet captures, VPCE flow logs, and sample request IDs.
2026-03-10 15:40 - Customer (NeonHealth NetOps): Uploaded pcap and VPCE access logs. Suspicious Set-Cookie headers added by our WAF; we rolled back the profile at 14:55 and errors decreased.
2026-03-10 17:10 - Support (Aisha): Confirmed serving nodes observed multiple upstream reconnections showing HTTP/1.1 semantics; forwarding to SRE for deeper analysis. Assigned to Oliver.

2026-03-11 09:20 - SRE (Oliver): Reproduced in lab by simulating a proxy that strips HTTP/2 framing and injects Set-Cookie. Observed KV-cache fragmentation and auth token validation errors on resumed connections.

2026-03-11 12:35 - Customer (NeonHealth SecOps): Provided firewall policy name 'WAF-INSPECT-COOKIE-AFFINITY' which was applied starting 2026-03-09 02:00 UTC. They scheduled a controlled rollback and will test in canary.
2026-03-12 08:05 - Support (Aisha): Customer rolled back the WAF rule in production canary and reported >90% reduction in streaming resets. Working with them to plan permanent mitigations.
2026-03-13 10:55 - SRE (Oliver): Documented workaround and requested follow-up: add an ingress health-check to detect HTTP/1.x re-serialization, update runbook, and add detection alert.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: WAF performing full HTTP reserialization for inspection inserts Set-Cookie and rewrites Connection semantics which breaks long-lived HTTP/2 multiplexed gRPC streams and causes session stickiness to fail.

Checked serving-runtime logs: when client connection recreated as HTTP/1.1, token refresh requests arrive on a new connection lacking previous connection-level KV-cache mapping -> auth verification fails intermittently.
Recreation: lab proxy that converts h2 -> h1 for a subset of streams reproduces RST_STREAM + 401 behaviour and increases per-request KV-cache misses by ~20%.

Correlation found between number of concurrent long streams and probability of downgrade: proxy had per-connection buffer limits and serialized some streams to new HTTP/1.1 sessions causing affinity mismatches.
VPCE flow logs show mixed ALPN; some client endpoints fall back to h2 while intermediate appliance uses HTTP/1.1 for downstream uplinks. This path mismatch correlates with failed resumption tokens.
Risk: Persistent cookie injection + HTTP/2 reserialization leads to higher auth churn and increased operational cost for customer (retries, token exchanges).
resolution:
Short term: Customer disabled the WAF cookie-affinity profile which removed header injection and eliminated HTTP/2 -> HTTP/1.1 reserialization; incident impact dropped to negligible.

Medium/long term recommended actions:
- Customer: configure WAF to preserve ALPN and avoid HTTP/2 reserialization for traffic to Redwood endpoints or add explicit bypass for Redwood hostnames.
- Redwood: add ingress detection that flags mixed HTTP/2/HTTP/1.1 ALPN for a single client IP and surface an alert; create runbook for Support to triage header injection/use of cookie-affinity appliances.
- Engineering follow-up: evaluate making token resumption more robust to connection rebinds (INT task recommended).

Permanent fix status: awaiting customer confirmation on final WAF policy change. If customer cannot change WAF behavior, Redwood can offer an alternative: a dedicated private NAT gateway or static egress path (Dedicated plan discussion).
